interpretation: The note, attached to the sentence of §3 calling the first believers 'the ἐκκλησία τοῦ θεοῦ ... kings and priests unto God', says that the designation of the Christian community as ἐκκλησία perhaps originates with Paul, and that 'the words of the Lord, Matt. XVI. 18; XVIII. 17, belong to a later period'. Read as: the two sayings, and not only their vocabulary, were formed after Jesus, so that Jesus did not give the ekklēsia the hearing and excluding power Matthew 18.17 reports. The event-level reading is chosen because Harnack's §2 (II. Details, 7; claim HARNACK-HOD-I-II-2-NO-NEW-COMMUNITY-PREACHING-COMMISSION) denies that Jesus founded a community at all, so a wording-only reading (the term is late, the conferral on a community might be Jesus') does not fit his position; that reading is recorded as rejected in ATTEMPT-GOVERNING-COMMISSION-ATTESTATION. It is stronger than the note's words in one step: from the dating of the saying to the non-occurrence of the conferral (Commissioning.Gave, which includes a promise); that step is this claim's reading, supported by §2, not stated in note 76. The wording-only reading remains a recorded alternative, rejected for Harnack's position as a whole, not for the note in isolation. The reading is weaker than the source in two ways: the statement encodes only 18.17, because 16.18 (the promise to build the ekklēsia on the rock) names no power given to a disciple and so is not in the commission vocabulary; and the note's dating of 16.18 bears on stage 5 (STMT-CHRIST-FOUNDED-VISIBLE-CHURCH), not on this statement. The note gives no argument for the dating, and it does not mention Matthew 16.19, 18.18, John 20.23 or John 21.15-17; nothing is attributed to Harnack about those verses. Harnack is a historian's reconstruction; the claim records that a pinned source states the denial, not that it is true. Basis: Buchanan's English translation named in the passage manifest.
